slides.say: In Daniel's class, one fifth of the students are boys who play basketball, and among those, one third also play the guitar. What could be the number of students in the class?

So we don't know the size of the class, and they ask what it could be. So we don't look for the number itself, we rule out what it can't be. And look at the fractions. There's no such thing as a fifth of a student. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, step by step with the fractions, and then by building the class from the inside.

[short pause] Let's start step by step. A fifth of the class are basketball boys, and a fifth of a class has to be a whole number of kids. So the class is divisible by five. And remember the sign for five, the last digit is zero or five.
at: So the class is divisible by five

slides.say: Thirty-five ends in five, and forty-five ends in five, so they stay. Forty-two and thirty-two don't, so choice numbers three and four are out.

Now the second fraction. A third of the basketball boys play the guitar. So it is the basketball group, not just the whole class, that must be divisible by three. With thirty-five students, thirty-five over five gives seven basketball boys. Seven cannot be split into three equal whole-number groups of students. So this class size does not work, and choice number one is out.
So forty-five is the only one left, and choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to build the class from the inside, from the smallest group out. Call the guitar players k, a whole number of kids. They're a third of the basketball boys, so there are three k basketball boys. And the basketball boys are a fifth of the class, so the class is five times three k, which is fifteen k.

k is a whole number, so the class is always a multiple of fifteen. Here both fractions have one on top, one fifth and one third. For nested fractions like these, multiply the denominators. That is not a rule for every fraction of a fraction. Let's see the same idea with half of a quarter of a group. Two times four is eight, so the group divides by eight, not just by four. With eight kids, a quarter is two, and half of that is one.
at: both fractions have one on top

slides.say: So which choice is a multiple of fifteen? Fifteen, thirty, forty-five. Forty-five, choice number two. Thirty-five, forty-two and thirty-two aren't on that list.

slides: [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
